newsitem.title: CHINA: No sackings at China zinc smelter, says official.
newsitem.headline: No sackings at China zinc smelter, says official.

text.p: An official at the Zhuzhou zinc smelter in central Hunan province on Tuesday denied rumours of management changes at the factory.
The official, reached by telephone, was commenting on speculation that Zhuzhou managers had been removed from their jobs following big losses on the world zinc market.
The rumours began after an executive with a major supplier said a Western delegation scheduled to visit Zhuzhou next week had been told the trip was not timely because of management changes.
"They've had their visit cancelled, and that was basically the reason they were given," the supplier source told Reuters.
Officials at Beijing's central metals producing arm, China National Nonferrous Metals Corp (CNNC), said they had no information about management changes at Zhuzhou.
The rumours surfaced after news of major losses racked up by Zhuzhou and other Chinese smelters that sold forward hundreds of thousands of tonnes of zinc earlier this year on the advice of CNNC.

Zhuzhou built a short position of 90,000 tonnes of zinc on the London Metal Exchange (LME) after following CNNC's advice to sell forward once the price reached levels around $1,100 a tonne, Chinese sources have said.
The total Chinese short position was reported in an official Chinese magazine to be up to 250,000 tonnes. CNNC officials later confirmed the figure was around this level.
On the basis of the Chinese sales, zinc prices soared, early last week reaching seven-year highs of around $1,700, before collapsing on last Tuesday.
Since the fall, which saw zinc lose $300, or 20 percent, in an hour's trade last Tuesday, the price of the metal has settled in a range and on Monday closed up $31 at $1,494.
